analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: the open's +1.0% S&P gain has fully faded by mid-morning — the index is back below Wednesday's close, the Dow is -0.64%, and only the Nasdaq (+0.37%) is still green. The Mag 7 gains have roughly halved from their early readings, and Apple remains the lone persistent decliner. The earnings story is now two-sided and consistent: Walmart's beat-and-raise sold off, Williams-Sonoma's in-line quarter is down 9%, and Alibaba's revenue beat with an EPS miss slipped — the bar for retail and for AI spend is the profit line and the guide, not the top line. The one clean earnings winner is Palo Alto, and it is lifting all of cybersecurity. Healthcare is the second-day drag from the CMS Medicare Advantage proposal. Signal vs noise: the fade itself, the retail sell-the-news pattern, and the PANW sector lift are signal; the exact mid-morning Mag 7 percentages and the ANT opening print (still hours away) are noise until the close. The December hike case is unchanged — Jefferson's inflation framing stands, claims were soft-but-low, and Powell's speech this afternoon is the next real catalyst.

community_signals.takeaway: The 922-comment Anthropic IPO thread remains the live debate on the day's center of gravity, now reframed by the confirmed $83 price and the $26B supplier private placement: 'priced for perfection' skepticism at ~$1.5T vs AI-scarcity enthusiasm. It frames how the market may read ANT's first trade (~noon-1pm ET).
community_signals.title: Anthropic IPO

community_signals.takeaway: A research firm's 'unprecedented test of investor gullibility' framing of the IPO (217 comments) is the counterweight in the same debate — the valuation-versus-fundamentals argument that today's first trade will test.

headlines.headline: The morning rebound faded by mid-morning: S&P 500 7,317.63 (-0.08%), Nasdaq Composite 24,520.12 (+0.37%), Dow 49,879.03 (-0.64%) as of 10:31 AM ET (BestStocks/FMP) — down from +1.01% / +1.55% / +0.47% at the 9:31 AM ET open. The S&P is now below Wednesday's 7,323.63 close, so the five-day losing streak is not yet broken.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open pop did not hold into the late morning — the turn is still unconfirmed, and the close will decide whether this is a durable reversal or another fade into the Anthropic debut.

headlines.headline: Mag 7 mid-morning (Finnhub, 10:57 AM ET): Microsoft $517.72 (+1.85%), Nvidia $152.44 (+0.98%), Amazon $267.95 (+0.08%), Meta $616.03 (-0.06%), Apple $349.38 (-0.87%). Alphabet +3.88% to $293.41 and Tesla +0.45% per the 9:55-9:59 AM ET snapshots — all well off their early highs (MSFT was +3.04%, GOOGL ~+4% at the open).
headlines.why_it_matters: Six of seven are still green but the gains are shrinking through the morning — the AI-led rebound is narrowing, with Apple the persistent drag for a second straight session.

headlines.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) holding ~$152.44 (+0.98%) at 10:57 AM ET, above the $150 level after Wednesday's -2.9% close to $150.96 erased the post-earnings gain. Record Q3 stands (revenue $115.84B, +103% YoY; EPS $2.68 vs $2.47; Q4 guide $130B), but the leadership question and target cuts (UBS $220, Jefferies $250, Mizuho $220, Morgan Stanley $260, Piper $230) still cap the stock.
headlines.why_it_matters: Holding above $150 into the late morning is the first sign the floor may stick — but the fade from the +3% early heatmap reading shows buyers are still hesitant while the CEO search is open.

headlines.headline: Williams-Sonoma (WSM) extends its slide to -9.09% ($236.44) at 10:57 AM ET after Q3 results: non-GAAP EPS $2.19 vs $2.18 expected (in-line), revenue $1.99B vs ~$2.00B expected (a $10M miss), comps +5.1%, GAAP EPS $2.38 (+21.4%, helped by $29.3M in tariff refunds). FY26 outlook reiterated, not raised.
headlines.why_it_matters: An in-line quarter with a reiterated outlook is being sold hard — same pattern as Walmart's beat-and-raise selloff: the market is grading retail on the profit line and the guide, not the headline beat, into the holidays.

headlines.headline: Alibaba (BABA) reported its September quarter before the open: revenue CN¥271.5B (+10% YoY, just above estimates), but adjusted EPS CN¥8.10 missed the CN¥11.16 consensus; AI Cloud & Compute Services revenue +53% YoY and recurring revenue from external cloud customers +67%. Shares were down ~2% premarket from Wednesday's $84.37 close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Cloud is growing fast but the EPS miss shows the AI buildout is still costing more than it returns — the same capex-versus-profit tension hanging over the US hyperscalers, now with US chip-curb overhang on top.

headlines.headline: UnitedHealth (UNH) -3.97% at 10:31 AM ET and healthcare broadly weak (sector -1.26% on the 9:55 AM heatmap) after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services proposed an expanded anti-fraud rule (CMS-6098-P) targeting Medicare Advantage overpayments, per reports cited by Yahoo Finance. Managed care fell Wednesday too (HUM -13.0%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A regulatory overhang is hitting the whole managed-care group for a second day — it is the main non-tech drag on the Dow and on breadth while tech rallies.

headlines.headline: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) +3.61% to $352.19 at 10:31 AM ET, cooling from the +7-9% premarket surge after its beat-and-raise (fiscal Q1 revenue $3.445B, +39% YoY; adj EPS $1.05 vs $0.97; FY27 guide lifted; $4.5B Applied Compute acquisition). Cybersecurity is still lifting the sector: CrowdStrike +6.02%, Zscaler +6.89%, Okta +7.58%, Rubrik +8.46%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The strongest earnings catalyst of the morning is still working, just at half strength — a sector-wide lift on a clean beat-and-raise is the clearest 'earnings matter' signal in an otherwise fading tape.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) first trade still pending — expected around noon-1pm ET on the Nasdaq after the opening auction clears. IPO priced at $83 (above the $70-78 range) in an $81B offering, ~$1.5T valuation; the $26B supplier private placement (Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom $1B, Micron $1B, Microsoft $1B, TSMC $0.5B) and 315M day-one-eligible insider shares frame the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Still the day's center of gravity — the first trade prices whether the AI supply chain buying its biggest customer's equity is partnership or circularity, and the morning fade means ANT opens into a softer tape than the open suggested.
